Article Title: Quote of the day by Bhagat Singh: ‘Study so that you are able to meet the arguments of your opponents,’ and why knowledge is the strongest answer to disagreement
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Bhagat Singh

“Study so that you are able to meet the arguments of your opponents.” —

Bhagat Singh

Reading broadens the argument before it strengthens it

Knowledge changes the quality of disagreement

Why the quote still matters

Every disagreement presents a choice. One person raises their voice, while another repeats familiar slogans. A third begins asking questions, searching for evidence and trying to understand where the other side is coming from before responding. Bhagat Singh's advice belongs firmly in the third tradition. He treats study as preparation for conversation rather than examination, and knowledge as something that sharpens judgement instead of feeding pride. His words suggest that the strength of an argument depends less on confidence than on how carefully it has been built.Bhagat Singh wrote constantly throughout his short life. While imprisoned, he read history, economics, political philosophy, literature and revolutionary thought with remarkable discipline, filling notebooks with quotations and reflections from writers across the world. His reading shaped his politics, though it also shaped the way he argued. He believed conviction carried greater weight when it rested on careful thought instead of emotion alone. That is why this line continues to resonate. It speaks to anyone who hopes to persuade rather than simply win.People usually begin with opinions. Study asks them to examine where those opinions come from. A reader who spends time with different authors soon discovers that intelligent people have disagreed about almost every important question in history.Freedom, justice, religion, economics and education have all been debated across generations, often by thinkers who arrived at very different conclusions while drawing on equally serious scholarship.That process does something valuable. It slows certainty. Someone who has read widely becomes more careful with conclusions because they understand how many perspectives exist beyond their own experience. A lawyer prepares by studying both sides of a case. A scientist examines competing explanations before accepting one. A historian compares sources instead of relying on a single account. Strong arguments grow from that habit of testing ideas before defending them.Bhagat Singh encouraged the same discipline. He wanted young people to read because reading develops the habit of thinking independently. A belief borrowed from someone else can be repeated. A belief reached through study can be explained, defended and refined.Modern life makes it easy to respond immediately. Social media rewards quick reactions, television debates often value interruption over discussion and public conversations frequently become contests of personality rather than ideas. In that environment, Bhagat Singh's advice feels remarkably current.Knowledge does not eliminate disagreement. It changes the way disagreement is handled. A person who understands the history behind an issue is less likely to reduce it to slogans. Someone familiar with evidence can separate facts from assumptions. Even when no agreement is reached, the conversation becomes more useful because each side has something substantial to contribute.Many of history's greatest debates produced progress because participants challenged one another with ideas rather than insults. Scientific discoveries emerged through criticism. Constitutional democracies developed through public debate. Universities exist because questioning accepted wisdom has always been considered an essential part of learning. Those traditions survive only when people value understanding as much as persuasion.Education is often treated as a path towards employment, and it certainly serves that purpose. Bhagat Singh points to another purpose that receives far less attention. Reading equips people to think clearly when confronted with difficult questions. It teaches them to recognise weak reasoning, appreciate strong evidence and remain open to learning even while defending deeply held beliefs.That lesson extends far beyond politics. Families resolve differences through conversation. Workplaces depend on people exchanging ideas without resentment. Democracies function because citizens weigh competing arguments before making choices. In each of those settings, knowledge becomes more than personal achievement.It becomes a public responsibility.Bhagat Singh's words endure because they place faith in the power of ideas. They remind readers that disagreement has never been settled by volume alone. Lasting influence belongs to those who understand an issue well enough to answer it with reason, evidence and the patience to keep learning.
Article Summary: Bhagat singh wrote constantly throughout his short life. While imprisoned, he read history, economics, political philosophy, literature and revolutionary thought. His reading shaped his politics, though it also shaped the way he argued. He wanted young people to read because reading develops the habit of thinking independently.

Article Title: 'May do same with Army': Opposition attacks BJP for India Hockey's saffron jersey
Article Text:
Oppn attacks BJP over hockey jersey colour change to saffron

Why was the jersey changed?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Opposition on Thursday targeted Centre over the change in the hockey teams' jersey colour from the traditional blue to saffron and expressed concerns that the army's uniform could be next target.The group also accused the BJP and the RSS of trying to impose saffron across institutions.The remarks came after Hockey India unveiled new saffron jerseys for the national men's and women's teams ahead of next month's FIH Hockey World Cup in the Netherlands and Belgium. Hockey India has said the change was made following feedback from players and coaches, who felt the blue jersey blended with the blue synthetic turf, affecting on-field visibility.Reacting to the development, Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra alleged that the BJP and RSS were attempting to reshape institutions and history."Whether they change uniforms or try to rewrite history through education policy, no matter what they do... You have seen what the youth of our country think about this. You heard what the young people gathered at Jantar Mantar were saying. This is the voice of the nation.The struggle for this country's independence was founded on non-violence and truth; the RSS played no part in it," she said."The entire nation knows the reality, and those who didn't are now realising what their true intentions are. The Congress party led that movement under the guidance of Mahatma Gandhi, and the very soul of this country is rooted in non-violence, truth, and brotherhood. No one can take that away—not the RSS, nor anyone else. No matter how much they sow division, incite violence, or spread hatred, the country's soul—defined by brotherhood, mutual love, and unity—remains intact; they cannot strip that away," she added.Congress MP Amar Singh accused the BJP of attempting to 'saffronise' everything."Today they have done this with hockey; tomorrow they may do the same with the Army. How can anyone trust them? They want saffron everywhere," he said.Calling the move 'very unfortunate', Singh said no political party should change symbols that carry historical significance."Everything has its own history and significance. But they simply do not stop. What can we do?" he added.Congress leader Tariq Anwar also criticised the decision, saying it reflected the BJP's 'narrow-minded ideology'."Whether it is in the field of education or other sectors, there is an attempt to impose a particular ideology everywhere. This controversy is a symbol of that narrow-minded thinking," he said.Trinamool Congress leader Kirti Azad, however, said a team's performance mattered more than the colour of its jersey."As for the orange colour versus green, that doesn't really matter. Performance should matter on the field. Even in cricket, we used to play in white clothes. It does not come from colours; it comes from performance," he said."You achieve it through your own effort. So, it is not about the colour of the clothes; it is about your ability in the sport," Azad added.At the same time, he questioned the need to replace the traditional blue jersey."If blue has traditionally been the colour associated with our sports, then it should remain so. Why impose a religious colour on it?" he said.Hockey India has defended the move, saying the decision was based on technical feedback from players and coaches, who found that the blue jersey merged with the blue synthetic playing surface used in international hockey, affecting visibility during matches.The federation said saffron was chosen after considering several alternative colours, adding that it also symbolises courage, sacrifice and national pride as one of the colours of the Indian national flag.The new jersey will be worn by both the men's and women's teams during the FIH Hockey World Cup, scheduled to be held in the Netherlands and Belgium from August 15 to 30.Former India captain Viren Rasquinha had criticised the move, saying the blue jersey represented the team's legacy and identity, while Hockey India maintained that changes in jersey colours were not unprecedented, observing that the national team had previously worn yellow in the 2014 World Cup and sky blue in the 2018 edition.
Article Summary: Oppn attacks bjp over hockey jersey colour change to saffron. Congress leader priyanka gandhi vadra alleged that the bjp and rss were attempting to reshape institutions and history. Hockey india said the change was made following feedback from players and coaches, who felt the blue jersey blended with the blue synthetic turf.

Article Title: Cristina Ulbrich’s cause of death: How did the wife of Atlanta Falcons defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich die?
Article Text:
Cristina Ulbrich and Jeff Ulbrich. Image via: Getty Images

What is Cristina Ulbrich's cause of death ?

Jeff Ulbrich's football journey has been shaped by family support

Falcons rally around the Ulbrich family during training camp

Cristina Ulbrich has passed away; the Atlanta Falcons confirmed Thursday while announcing the demise of the wife of defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich. The organization said Cristina died after a courageous battle, bringing heartbreaking news to the Falcons during the opening week of training camp.The announcement also explained Jeff Ulbrich's absence from practices earlier this week. While the Falcons continue preparations for the 2026 NFL season under new head coach Kevin Stefanski, the focus has shifted from football to supporting one of the franchise's longest-serving coaches and his family during an immeasurable loss.Cristina Ulbrich passed away after battling cancer, according to an official statement released by the Falcons. The team shared that she died on Sunday before publicly announcing the news later in the week.In its statement, the organization wrote:"The Atlanta Falcons are heartbroken by the passing of Cristina Ulbrich, beloved wife of defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich, after her courageous battle with cancer."The statement continued by highlighting the impact she had beyond her immediate family."Cristina was a devoted wife, mother, and friend whose strength, grace, and resilience touched all who knew her.She was a constant source of love and support to Jeff, their family, and the broader Falcons community."The Falcons also asked for privacy as the family grieves."On behalf of the entire organization, we extend our deepest condolences to Jeff, their children, and all who loved Cristina. During this incredibly difficult time, our thoughts and prayers are with the Ulbrich family. We ask that their privacy be respected as they grieve this profound loss, and we stand with them in support and remembrance of Cristina's life."Jeff Ulbrich had not been present during Tuesday's and Wednesday's training camp practices, with multiple reports describing his absence as being for personal reasons. The team's announcement later provided the reason.Jeff and Cristina Ulbrich shared three children, Samantha, Jax and Jace. According to The Athletic, the couple first met during Ulbrich's recruiting visit to the University of Hawaii in 1997, beginning a relationship that remained a constant throughout his playing and coaching career.After spending 10 seasons as a linebacker with the San Francisco 49ers, Ulbrich moved into coaching with the Seattle Seahawks before joining the UCLA Bruins. His NFL coaching career took off with the Falcons in 2015, where he eventually became assistant head coach and later defensive coordinator under interim coach Raheem Morris.Ulbrich later reunited with Robert Saleh on the New York Jets' staff in 2021 and served as interim head coach in 2024 after Saleh's dismissal. He returned to Atlanta as defensive coordinator and remained in the role after the Falcons hired Kevin Stefanski to lead the franchise for the 2026 season.Cristina's passing has resonated throughout the Falcons organization, where Jeff Ulbrich has earned respect during two separate coaching stints. The franchise's support extended beyond its initial announcement, with owner Arthur Blank also paying tribute to Cristina's life and influence.Blank said: "It was always evident how deeply Cristina loved her family and how fiercely she supported them. She faced every challenge with extraordinary courage, strength and grace, inspiring so many through the way she lived and the way she fought. My family and I, along with the entire Falcons family, send our love and prayers for strength to everyone mourning her loss."The Falcons are expected to continue training camp preparations while giving Ulbrich the time and privacy he needs.
Article Summary: Cristina ulbrich passed away after battling cancer, according to the atlanta falcons. The organization said cristina died after a courageous battle. The announcement also explained jeffulbrich's absence from practices earlier this week. The falcons continue preparations for the 2026 nfl season under kevin stefanski.

Jonathan Kuminga's free agency has turned into a two-team race, and both sides have reportedly landed on the same number. The Cleveland Cavaliers and Los Angeles Lakers are said to have capped their offers for the forward at around $18 million annually, well below the $20 million-plus he initially sought after Atlanta declined his $24.3 million team option.Cleveland has already met with Kuminga's side to work toward a sign-and-trade framework, and with Donovan Mitchell now locked up on a four-year extension and Cleveland working to re-sign James Harden, adding a 23-year-old wing with championship pedigree would address one of the roster's clearest needs. Whether Kuminga is willing to come down to Cleveland's number is now the deciding factor.Cleveland entered this offseason searching for a long-term wing and instead watched its roster thin out further. Dean Wade left for the Philadelphia 76ers, Keon Ellis signed with the Brooklyn Nets, and Larry Nance Jr. returned to the Indiana Pacers for a second stint elsewhere. The Cavaliers answered with depth moves like Thomas Bryant and Mario Hezonja rather than a wing solution, leaving the position still open.Kuminga, meanwhile, played just 16 games for Atlanta after arriving in a deal that sent Kristaps Porzingis to Golden State, averaging 13.7 points, 3.3 rebounds and an assist in the team's series against the New York Knicks.The Hawks declined his option rather than pay $24.3 million, pushing him onto the open market at 23 years old with real upside still ahead of him."The Cavaliers will meet with Jonathan Kuminga about working towards finalizing a potential sign-and-trade agreement soon, per Chris Fedor. Cleveland is a main finalist for Kuminga's services alongside the Lakers. Kuminga continues to seek a deal exceeding $20 million annually," NBA reporter Evan Sidery shared.The framework being discussed would have Cleveland structure a sign-and-trade with Atlanta, since the Hawks are already over the roster limit and need the move to return usable value rather than simply losing Kuminga for nothing. Names like Max Strus and Dennis Schröder have been mentioned as pieces Cleveland could send back to make the math work, though nothing has been confirmed as a finalized package.The appeal for Cleveland goes beyond need. Kuminga was on Golden State's title-winning roster before his move to Atlanta, and head coach Kenny Atkinson was part of that Warriors staff. That shared history is viewed as a real factor in Cleveland's pitch, giving the Cavaliers a relationship angle the Lakers can't match.Kuminga gives Cleveland a young, athletic wing still on the rise, a clear upgrade over the depth pieces the Cavaliers have retained this offseason. Slotting him alongside James Harden, assuming Cleveland re-signs him, would give Kuminga an established playmaker to work off of while he continues developing as a scorer.Financially, locking Kuminga in around the reported $15-18 million range rather than his original $20 million-plus ask would let Cleveland add the piece without blowing past its intended spending level, especially with Mitchell's extension now on the books.Cleveland's existing relationship through Kenny Atkinson and its reported asset advantage in sign-and-trade talks give it a real edge over the Lakers, but the gap between Kuminga's original ask and both teams' $18 million ceiling remains the biggest unresolved variable in this rumor.

Article Title: 'We've shared the dressing room for so many years': Rohit Sharma's heartfelt note for Ajinkya Rahane

NEW DELHI: Ajinkya Rahane announced his retirement from international cricket on Thursday, bringing the curtain down on a career that spanned nearly two decades. The veteran batter shared an emotional video on Instagram to announce his decision and soon received heartfelt tributes from across the cricketing world, including from his Mumbai teammate and former India captain Rohit Sharma Rohit praised Rahane's hard work and commitment, while thanking him for his contribution to Indian cricket."We've shared the dressing room for so many years, and I know how much hard work has gone into everything you've achieved. Your commitment and professionalism have always set you apart. Congratulations on a wonderful career. Best wishes," Rohit wrote in an X post.Rahane represented India in 85 Tests, scoring 5,077 runs, including 12 centuries and 26 fifties, at an average of 38.46.In ODIs, he played 90 matches and scored 2,962 runs, with three centuries and 24 fifties at an average of 35.26.In T20Is, Rahane featured in 20 matches and scored 375 runs, including one half-century.As India's Test captain, he remained unbeaten, recording four wins and two draws. He also has the highest win percentage among Indian Test captains who have led the team in at least five matches.One of Rahane's finest moments as captain came during the 2020-21 Border-Gavaskar Trophy.After India's heavy defeat in Adelaide, he led the team to a memorable comeback, guiding them to a Boxing Day Test win in Melbourne before sealing a historic series victory at the Gabba, where Australia's long unbeaten streak came to an end. Rahane also captained India to a crucial Test victory against Australia in Dharamshala in 2017.
Article Summary: Ajinkya rahane retires from international cricket. Rahane played 85 tests, scoring 5,077 runs, including 12 centuries and 26 fifties. He captained india to a crucial test victory against australia in 2017.

NEW DELHI: Neeraj Chopra qualified for the men's javelin throw final at the Commonwealth Games 2026 despite difficult weather conditions in Glasgow. After finishing fifth in the qualification round with a best throw of 79.61m, the Olympic champion said the cold and changing winds made it tough for all athletes.However, he was happy that all three Indian javelin throwers reached the final.Neeraj did enough to secure his place in the 12-man final with a best throw of 79.61m at Scotstoun Stadium. In the gold medal match, he will compete against defending Commonwealth champion Arshad Nadeem, Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, world champion Keshorn Walcott and former world champion Anderson Peters.India's Rohit Yadav and Yash Vir Singh also qualified, giving India three medal hopes in the final.Neeraj said he was not looking for a huge throw in the qualification round. His main aim was to book a place in the final.“It was really cold and windy, but the throw was okay, the 79m throw. The goal was to go in the final and give my best in the final, so I'm happy with the throw,” Neeraj said.“Conditions are not best for javelin throwers. Not only cold, but it's really windy. The wind was also not in the front; sometimes it's from the side. It's really hard to process where we have to throw. Sometimes we think, ‘Okay, we'll throw there’, but then the wind comes from the other side. And lots of throwers are struggling today. Nobody touched the automatic qualification mark. It was tough conditions, but we are happy that all three Indians are in the final,” he said.Neeraj believes the final will be of a very high standard as several top javelin throwers from around the world will be competing for medals.“Yeah, it's a crazy field. For an event like Javelin Throw, that will be a really good final. Hope conditions will be okay tomorrow. Everyone looks in good shape. Let's see tomorrow.”Neeraj also praised Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, calling him one of the brightest young talents in the sport. He said it is good to see javelin becoming more popular in South Asia.“He's the new kid on the block, the rising star. He throws really well. He's a good friend of mine. This year he has thrown really well. It's good that Javelin is growing in our neighbourhood. It feels good that he did something great for Sri Lanka.”Neeraj said javelin has become much more popular in recent years. Better coaching, improved facilities and easy access to training information have helped young athletes take up the sport.“Javelin is really popular in South Asia now. There are lots of Javelin throwers. There are lots of athletes, and they are training for Javelin. So there is a better chance that so many good athletes will come. Earlier, Javelin as a sport was not that famous. But in the last few years, people support javelin and people know about the sport. So they know there is a future, and they really push themselves.“We have good facilities now, and we know about javelin. Because when I started, I didn't know how we had to plan for Javelin training and how we had to train. But right now, because of the internet, you can know about Javelin training. So it's really good that people know about Javelin now. That's why people recognise Javelin throw, and they try to give their best.”Neeraj said winning the gold medal at the Tokyo Olympics helped increasein javelin across India. He added that the country now has many athletes capable of throwing beyond 80 metres.“Earlier, there were lots of other really good athletes that provided a boost to other sports. But after my Tokyo Olympics gold, there was an immense boost in Javelin. I'm happy we have really good throwers now. I think we have around 20 80m throwers, so it’s really good for India,” Chopra concluded.
Article Summary: Neeraj chopra qualified for the men's javelin throw final at the commonwealth games 2026. Olympic champion finished fifth in the qualification round with a best throw of 79.61m. Rohit and Yash Vir complete Indian clean sweep

NEW DELHI: Two-time Olympic medallist Neeraj Chopra led a clean sweep for India in the men's javelin throw qualification at the Commonwealth Games 2026, with all three Indian throwers advancing to the medal round in Glasgow on Thursday.Joining the former Commonwealth Games champion in the final were Rohit Yadav and Yash Vir Singh, ensuring a full Indian contingent in the title-deciding contest scheduled for Friday.Competing in chilly conditions at Scotstoun Stadium, Chopra adopted a cautious approach as he continued his comeback from a long-term back injury.The 2018 Commonwealth Games gold medallist opened with a modest 76.28m, placing sixth after the opening round. He improved to 79.61m with his second throw to climb to fifth and, with qualification already secured, chose to skip his final attempt.Despite receiving the loudest cheers from the crowd while sporting a beanie in the cold Glasgow weather, Chopra focused on doing just enough to progress rather than chasing a big mark.Difficult conditions played a major role throughout the event. With a steady headwind and temperatures around 18 degrees Celsius, none of the competitors managed to breach the automatic qualifying standard of 84m, meaning the top 12 athletes advanced to the final based on their rankings.Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage, winner of this season's Doha and Rome Diamond League meetings, topped the qualification with a first-round effort of 82.84m.India's other two representatives also safely negotiated the qualification round.Rohit Yadav, who boasts a personal and season best of 87.05m, began with 77.04m before improving to 78.37m in his second attempt. Like Chopra, he skipped his final throw after confirming his place in the medal round, finishing ninth overall.Yash Vir Singh, whose personal best stands at 83.72m, improved steadily through the competition. The 24-year-old opened with 73.89m, followed it up with 74.45m, and then produced 78.36m with his final attempt to finish 10th and seal qualification.Chopra is competing in his first Commonwealth Games since winning gold at Gold Coast 2018, having missed the Birmingham 2022 edition because of injury.The former world champion only returned to competition earlier this season after recovering from a persistent lower-back injury that had sidelined him since September last year. He made his comeback at the Doha Diamond League in June, finishing fourth with a best throw of 85.69m.With all three Indians safely through, the focus now shifts to the final, where Chopra will look to reclaim the Commonwealth Games crown while Rohit and Yash Vir aim to challenge for podium finishes and complete a memorable outing for India.
Article Summary: Two-time olympic medallist neeraj chopra led a clean sweep for india in the men's javelin throw qualification at the commonwealth games 2026. Joining the former commonwealth games champion in the final were rohit yadav and yash vir singh, ensuring a full indian contingent in the title-deciding contest.

The WNBA's own account is the reason Angel Reese and Paige Bueckers are facing gambling questions this week. During All-Star Weekend, the two stars made a friendly $400 bet on which of their teams would win Wednesday's Wings-Dream game, and the league's social media team filmed and posted it, quoting Bueckers on the terms of the wager.The post ran straight into the WNBA's own rulebook. Section 5(c) of the CBA prohibits players from wagering money or anything of value on the outcome of league games, and the clip showed cash changing hands on camera. The league pulled the video within hours, but by then it had already been screenshotted and recirculated widely.The backlash centered on a simple problem: the league's own staff had broadcast conduct that its own agreement forbids. Fans didn't need to dig for the CBA language once people started pointing it out, and the quiet deletion only made the clip more visible.That leaves commissioner Cathy Engelbert with an awkward choice. Disciplining two of the league's most marketable young players over content her own team promoted risks looking heavy-handed. Ignoring it risks signaling the rulebook only applies when convenient. Either way, the original misstep sits with the league office, not the players who agreed to a $400 bet on camera.The reaction online was immediate and unsparing. Fox Sports host Clay Travis wrote:@ClayTravis shared: "I can’t even comprehend how dumb you have to be to post this video from the league’s official account. Like sub 70 IQ. And how stupid are the players too?! On video bets with cash being shown?"Others zeroed in on the enforcement gap. One user, @krk73, wrote:"Endorsing? Pardon....They aren't endorsing players betting on games. The players are literally betting on games on camera."Another, @SachaVeldhuis, predicted nothing would come of it:"So thats a fine or suspension. But nothing wil happen, all jokes. How dumb is this league. Players getting threats from sports bettors. Tonedeaf league."Several fans also raised double-standard questions, asking whether Fever players would have faced faster discipline for the same clip.Wednesday's game gave the story a second act. In the first quarter at College Park Center, Bueckers switched onto Reese in the post. Reese drove at the smaller Bueckers, who forced a turnover and drew a foul in the process, then celebrated the stop by clapping directly at Reese. Reese approached her, words were exchanged, and no technical foul was called on either player. Dallas carried a 38-32 lead into halftime.The two are reportedly friendly away from the court, having spent time together during All-Star Weekend just days earlier. Reese has drawn attention for in-game needling before, and Bueckers isn't a stranger to it either. Whether the league addresses the wager before their next meeting remains the open question hanging over both teams.

Article Title: Lamine Yamal's net worth at 19 reveals how far he has come from a childhood of struggle and poverty
Article Text:
Lamine Yamal's struggle and net worth (Getty Images)

What is Lamine Yamal's net worth right now?

How much does Lamine Yamal earn from sponsorships and brand deals?

Where did Lamine Yamal grow up and how did his family get to Spain?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lamine Yamal is 19, a World Cup winner, and sitting on an estimated net worth of something many can only dream of in their lifetime. That figure is only going to grow. In May 2025, Barcelona handed him a six-year contract worth $18 million annually before tax, a deal that landed him tenth on Forbes' list of football's highest earners. The same boy who once slept in an apartment where the bedroom and kitchen shared the same four walls is now one of the most commercially valuable teenagers the sport has ever produced.Celebrity Net Worth puts Lamine Yamal's current wealth at around $15 million, though that number already feels dated. His previous Barcelona contract paid him roughly $1.82 million per year. The club scrapped it. The new deal, signed in the summer of 2025, pays $18 million annually before tax, and that base figure rises further depending on performance bonuses and trophies collected along the way.Barcelona knew exactly what they were protecting. Yamal became the youngest player in the club's history to feature for the first team, doing so at 15 years, nine months, and 16 days. He is the youngest scorer ever for the Spanish national team, the youngest goalscorer in European Championship history, and at 17, the youngest player ever nominated for the Ballon d'Or. Those records are not decorative. They explain why Barcelona moved so fast to lock him down on a long-term deal.His salary is the headline, but the sponsorship income is where the real scale of Lamine Yamal's commercial reach becomes clear. His deal with Adidas is worth approximately $34 million over ten years, making it the anchor of a portfolio that also includes Beats by Dre, OPPO, Powerade, Konami, and UNICEF. For a teenager who has not yet hit his physical peak, that level of brand interest says something about how the market views his trajectory.Most players spend years building that kind of commercial profile. Yamal had it before he turned 18. Brands are not betting on who he is right now. They are betting on who he is going to be for the next decade, and so far, nothing in his career has given them a reason to doubt that investment.Lamine Yamal was born on July 13, 2007, in the Rocafonda neighbourhood of Mataró. His father, Mounir Nasraoui, worked as a building painter of Moroccan origin. His mother, Sheila Ebana, was a waitress from Equatorial Guinea. They separated when Lamine was three. The family lived modestly, in a small apartment where, as Yamal has since admitted, the kitchen and bedroom occupied the same space.The person who shaped him most was his grandmother, Fatima. She arrived in Spain from Morocco with nothing and built everything from scratch. Yamal spoke about it plainly during an appearance on the podcast Resonancia de Corazón con José Ramón de la Morena: "The first to arrive in Spain was my grandmother, who sneaked onto a bus coming from Morocco and managed to reach Mataró."He continued: "She started working 3 jobs so that my father could come, because he stayed in Morocco. And when my grandmother had saved some money, she paid a woman to bring my father and his sister, who came to Spain when they were three years old."That story of sacrifice, grinding and unglamorous, is what sits beneath all the contracts and endorsement deals. Yamal has been open about the fact that providing a more stable life for his family is the part of his success that means the most to him. The money matters. But it matters because of where it came from.
Article Summary: Lamine yamal is one of the most commercially valuable teenagers in football. The 19-year-old has signed a six-year contract with barcelona worth $18 million annually before tax. His current deal with adidas is worth approximately $34 million over ten years. His family came to spain from morocco when he was three years old.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Pablo Picasso: "When I was as old as these children, I could draw like Raphael, but it took me a lifetime to learn to…" - a profound lesson on creativity, simplicity and rediscover
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Pablo Picasso (Image: Wikipedia)

Quote of the day by Pablo Picasso

"When I was as old as these children, I could draw like Raphael, but it took me a lifetime to learn to draw like them"

What the quote actually means

Where this quote actually comes from

Why real mastery is more than technical skill

Why children create so freely in the first place

Why fear so often gets in the way of real creativity

Why simplicity is often the harder, more impressive achievement

Why curiosity should never really disappear with age

A note on Picasso's own artistic journey

Other memorable quotes by Pablo Picasso

"Everything you can imagine is real."

"Every child is an artist. The problem is how to remain an artist once we grow up."

"I paint objects as I think them, not as I see them."

"Learn the rules like a pro, so you can break them like an artist."

Why this quote is relevant

Quote of the day by Pablo Picasso: "When I was as old as these children, I could draw like Raphael, but it took me a lifetime to learn to…" - a profound lesson on creativity, simplicity and rediscovering the fearless artist withinChildren draw without hesitation, painting exactly what they imagine rather than what anyone expects of them. Pablo Picasso pointed at that exact quality with real admiration. "When I was as old as these children, I could draw like Raphael," he said, "but it took me a lifetime to learn to draw like them." A popular shortened version of this line, "it took me my whole life to learn to draw like a child," circulates far more widely, but it leaves out the actual comparison that gives the thought its real bite, the specific gap between a technique that took years to master and a freedom that came naturally to children without any training at all.Picasso is not claiming children's drawings are technically superior to a trained artist's work. He is admiring what sits behind them, working entirely without fear, experimenting freely, driven by imagination rather than any concern for getting things exactly right. As artists become more skilled, they tend to become far more aware of rules, expectations and the possibility of criticism. Picasso believed genuine creativity meant combining real technical mastery with that same fearless imagination children have naturally, before anyone has taught them to be self-conscious about it.The fuller version of this line, with the direct comparison to Raphael, is documented in Ingo F. Walther's book Picasso, part of the Basic Art series. The most widely repeated popular paraphrase reads, "It took me four years to paint like Raphael, but a lifetime to paint like a child," which trims the wording slightly differently but keeps the same essential comparison. The much shorter version usually quoted today, "it took me my whole life to learn to draw like a child," drops the Raphael reference entirely, which is really the detail that makes the original observation land properly, since it directly measures technical mastery against something children manage without ever being taught it at all.Most people assume expertise simply means becoming more precise over time. Picasso's own career complicates that idea directly. He had mastered classical, realistic drawing while still a teenager, essentially able to draw like Raphael long before he was an adult. Yet after reaching that level of technical ability, he spent decades deliberately simplifying his work and pushing into entirely new forms of expression. His own path shows that mastery was never only about knowing more. It was just as much about expressing an idea with real honesty and clarity, however simple the final result actually looked.Children rarely worry about making a mistake before they even start. They paint purple trees and flying elephants without a second thought, because they have not yet learned to fear being wrong about anything. That openness is exactly what allows genuine experimentation, and plenty of real breakthroughs in science, business and art begin with someone willing to ask a question that sounds a little unusual or unrealistic at first.As people get older, they tend to become far more preoccupied with how something will be judged. Will people approve of it. Will the idea simply fail. Will it make me look foolish. These worries discourage the kind of experimentation Picasso is describing, and his own quote is really an invitation to recover the confidence to explore an idea without letting perfectionism quietly block the way first.Complexity tends to impress people on the surface. Genuine simplicity usually requires a much deeper understanding underneath it. Whether in painting, writing or plain communication, expressing something genuinely meaningful in a clear, accessible way turns out to be remarkably difficult in practice. Picasso seemed to believe that simplicity earned through real experience represented a higher form of creativity than complexity created purely for its own sake.Children ask endless questions, why, how, what if, without any embarrassment about not already knowing the answer. Holding onto that same curiosity through adulthood tends to encourage genuine lifelong learning. People who keep exploring, questioning and experimenting well into their careers tend to stay more innovative than people who quietly stop asking those questions once they feel sufficiently expert.Picasso showed extraordinary technical skill from a genuinely young age, producing highly realistic paintings while still a teenager. Later, he became a pioneer of Cubism, continually reinventing his own artistic style across an unusually long career. His quote reflects the belief that while technique can be taught fairly directly, holding onto imagination, spontaneity and real originality is closer to a lifelong pursuit than a skill someone simply finishes learning.In a world that often rewards efficiency, correctness and simply fitting in, Picasso's line is a reminder of what imagination is actually worth, the courage to create freely, the willingness to get things wrong along the way, and the ability to see real possibility where other people only see limitations. None of that belongs exclusively to children. It stays available to anyone still willing to hold onto it.
Article Summary: Quote of the day by pablo picasso: "when i was as old as these children, i could draw like raphael, but it took me a lifetime to learn to draw like them" a profound lesson on creativity, simplicity and rediscovering the fearless artist within.

Why this quote is relevant

Watching a champion perform can make success look effortless, as though it were simply handed to a lucky few at birth. Tiger Woods pushed back on that idea directly. "Talent is something you are born with, and a skill is something you develop," he said. "99% of what you need to succeed in golf are skills." Talent might give someone a starting point. What actually determines how far they get is what they choose to practise and refine every single day after that, a lesson that Woods himself spent decades proving through his own extraordinarily disciplined career. What gives this quote unusual weight is that Woods didn't just say it once and move on. He proved it repeatedly, rebuilding his swing and his body after injury after injury, when relying purely on natural gift would have quietly ended his career years earlier."Talent is something you are born with, and a skill is something you develop. 99% of what you need to succeed in golf are skills"Woods draws a clear line between two very different things. Talent is natural ability, something someone may already have from a young age. Skill is something earned, built up through repetition, discipline, learning from mistakes and steady, continuous improvement, none of which arrives automatically no matter how talented someone started out.Saying that 99% of golfing success comes from skill is Woods arguing that raw natural ability, on its own, is almost never enough. Even the most naturally gifted players still need thousands of hours refining the basics and correcting weaknesses. The quote shifts attention away from what someone was simply born with and toward what they can actually control through effort.Woods has been blunt about his own background in the past. "People don't understand that when I grew up, I was never the most talented," he said. "I was never the biggest. I was never the fastest. I certainly was never the strongest. The only thing I had was my work ethic, and that's been what has gotten me this far." That is not a modest exaggeration. It is exactly the same claim the main quote is making, just told from the inside.Across a career spanning decades, Woods has won 15 major championships and 82 PGA Tour events, a total that ties him for the most wins in PGA Tour history. His success was never built on natural ability alone. It came from relentless practice, physical conditioning, mental preparation and constant technical adjustment, and after multiple serious injuries and surgeries, he rebuilt his game more than once through exactly the same patience and hard work his quote describes, refusing to simply rely on the natural gifts everyone assumed had carried him this far already.Natural talent might give someone a real head start early on, but skill keeps developing for as long as someone keeps working on it. A gifted musician still practises scales every day. An experienced surgeon still keeps learning new techniques years into their career. Nearly every profession rewards people who keep improving long after their natural strengths have already become obvious to everyone. Skill, unlike raw talent, is cumulative. Every hour spent genuinely learning adds a little more competence, confidence and consistency to what came before it.Potential only actually means something once it gets developed. Plenty of people with real natural gifts never fully use them because they lean too heavily on simply being gifted. Others, starting from a far more ordinary place, end up surpassing them purely through years of consistent practice. Sport shows this pattern constantly. Athletes with disciplined training habits generally outperform equally talented rivals who never prepared properly. The same pattern shows up in business, education, music and almost everywhere else too.Mastery rarely arrives through one dramatic breakthrough. It usually comes from repeating simple actions until they become second nature. Professional golfers spend enormous amounts of time on short putts, bunker shots and basic swing mechanics, and those small, repeated improvements are ultimately what separate elite performers from everyone else. The same is true elsewhere. Pilots rehearse emergency procedures long before they might ever need one. Excellence usually comes from repetition rather than a sudden flash of inspiration.Developing any real skill involves failing along the way, missed shots, disappointing rounds, rejected ideas. All of that failure carries useful information for anyone actually paying attention to it. Woods has spoken about analysing his own poor rounds directly rather than ignoring them, treating every mistake as part of the learning process rather than something to brush past.Motivation rises and falls depending on the day. Discipline is what keeps someone practising even once the initial enthusiasm has faded. People who wait to feel inspired before doing the work tend to make patchy, inconsistent progress. People who simply build a routine keep improving steadily regardless of how motivated they happen to feel on any given day.Modern culture tends to celebrate sudden success while skipping past the years of preparation that actually produced it. Woods' quote is a useful reminder that lasting achievement is usually built through steady, consistent effort rather than natural talent on its own. Talent might open the very first door. Skill is what actually decides how far someone gets to go after that, whatever field they happen to be working in.
